mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic demand, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 60-day horizon in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 8% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Unemployment rate rises above 8% but S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in unemployment and decreases in payroll employment indicate labor market distress, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Both unemployment increases and payroll employment decreases occur, yet S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, higher federal funds rates increase borrowing costs, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Federal funds rate exceeds 4% but S&P 500 returns remain positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Industrial production growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in CPI suggests inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by 0.5% in a month
failure_condition: CPI increases by 0.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Declines in both housing starts and retail sales signal weak demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Both housing starts and retail sales decline but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, slowing payroll employment growth signals potential economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Payroll employment growth slows but S&P 500 returns remain positive in more than 50% of cases.
